newsitem.title: UK: Lead to move closer to balance in 1997 - Brook Hunt.
newsitem.headline: Lead to move closer to balance in 1997 - Brook Hunt.

text.p: LONDON, Oct 7 - The Western world lead market is due to move closer into balance with 1996's deficit of 90,000 tonnes shrinking to a deficit of 17,000 tonnes next year, said Claire Hassall of analysts Brook Hunt.
Speaking at the LME metals week seminar, she forecast an average price of 37 cents per pound in 1996 rising to 39 cents per pound in 1997.
Mine production was set to increase seven percent from 2.1 million tonnes in 1996 to 2.25 million tonnes in 1997.

Total supplies of primary, secondary, net imports from East Bloc countries and U.S. government stockpile sales will total 5.027 million tonnes in 1996, rising to 5.223 million tonnes in 1997. Consumption is set to reach 5.1 million tonnes in 1996 and 5.24 million tonnes in 1997.
Hassall said China was the main uncertainty in the market and was expected to export 200,000 tonnes this year.
Chinese refined lead production rose 17 percent in the year to August, but was expected to rise 15 percent for the year overall, with a smaller two percent increase in 1997.
"The recent rise in exports has been at least in part from domestic inventory," Hassall said.
Regarding the world lead concentrate market, mine production has risen along with treatment charges.

"Concentrate supply is very definitely moving to surplus. But we do not see that secondary lead production will fall back in response to this," she said, suggesting that total lead production will rise.
